result.topic_en: A table stating, for prime divisors of the forms 4n±1, 8n±1, 8n±3, 12n±1, 12n±5, whether +1, -1, ±2, ±3 are quadratic residues or non-residues, followed by an inductive extension to ±5 for primes of forms 20n±1, 20n±9.
result.transcription:
PER NVMEROS PRIMOS. 131
Diuifor primus
$4n+1$ $\begin{cases} +1 \text{ refiduum} \\ -1 \text{ refiduum} \end{cases}$
$4n-1$ $\begin{cases} +1 \text{ refiduum} \\ -1 \text{ non-refid.} \end{cases}$
$8n+1$ $\begin{cases} +2 \text{ refiduum} \\ -2 \text{ refiduum} \end{cases}$
$8n-1$ $\begin{cases} +2 \text{ refiduum} \\ -2 \text{ non-refid.} \end{cases}$
$8n+3$ $\begin{cases} +2 \text{ non-refid.} \\ -2 \text{ refiduum} \end{cases}$
$8n-3$ $\begin{cases} +2 \text{ non-refid.} \\ -2 \text{ non-refid.} \end{cases}$
$12n+1$ $\begin{cases} +3 \text{ refiduum} \\ -3 \text{ refiduum} \end{cases}$
$12n-1$ $\begin{cases} +3 \text{ refiduum} \\ -3 \text{ non-refid.} \end{cases}$
$12n+5$ $\begin{cases} +3 \text{ non-refid.} \\ -3 \text{ non-refid.} \end{cases}$
$12n-5$ $\begin{cases} +3 \text{ non-refid.} \\ -3 \text{ refiduum.} \end{cases}$
Hinc per inductionem vlterius progredi licet hoc modo
Erit fi diuifor primus fit
$\begin{rcases} +5 \text{ refiduum} \\ -5 \text{ refiduum} \end{rcases}$ $20n+1;\ 20n+9$
$\begin{rcases} +5 \text{ refiduum} \\ -5 \text{ non-refid.} \end{rcases}$ $20n-1;\ 20n-9$
R 2 +5

items.quote: Hinc per inductionem vlterius progredi licet hoc modo
items.english: From here one may proceed further by induction in this way.
+5 and -5 are both residues if the prime divisor is of the form 20n+1 or 20n+9.
+5 is a residue and -5 a non-residue if the prime divisor is of the form 20n-1 or 20n-9.
